topicCandidates: Effective-dated immigration fees for change of status, extension of stay, permanent residence, re-entry permission, and certificates of authorized employment.
Consular visa issuance fees, nationality or purpose exceptions, local-currency collection, and separate approved-agency handling charges.
No-fee procedures that users may reasonably assume carry a charge, beginning with Certificate of Eligibility applications.
Material national, prefectural, municipal, school, housing, transport, document, tax, insurance, and private costs already implicated by canonical guidance.
A maintainable presentation contract that separates official fees, liabilities, variable charges, deposits, financial thresholds, estimates, and private prices.
userSituations: A permanent-residence applicant needs to know whether the current fee or the October 1, 2026 fee applies to an application already filed.
A resident comparing online and counter procedures needs to see the correct government fee, any processing charge, payment method, and when payment becomes due.
A visa applicant needs to distinguish a Japanese consular issuance fee from an agency handling charge and understand that nationality or purpose may change the amount.
A student or worker needs to know that the COE application itself has no government application fee while school, agent, translation, mailing, or professional charges may still exist.
A reader budgeting for a municipal, driving, housing, school, tax-document, or daily-life procedure needs a current official handoff when no national fixed price exists.
edgeCasesAndExceptions: The application acceptance date, not only the decision date, controls which immigration fee regime applies during a transition.
From October 1, 2026, change-of-status and extension fees vary by granted period; counter and online totals differ, and online payments include a separate processing charge.
Permanent residence is not an online procedure in the same way as eligible change or extension applications, and its fee must not be inferred from the online duration table.
Fee reductions or exemptions may apply in defined circumstances and require separate source-backed explanation.
Special re-entry permission and an ordinary re-entry permit are different procedures; a fee for one must not be attributed to the other.
A visa fee may be waived or differ by nationality or purpose, is collected in local currency, and may be accompanied by a separate approved-agency handling charge.
Taxes, health-insurance premiums, pension contributions, tuition, rent-related charges, and proof-of-funds thresholds are not application fees and often cannot be reduced to one national amount.
jurisdictionVariables: Application acceptance date, permission type, granted period of stay, counter or online channel, payment method, and any reduction or exemption.

Institution, provider, contract, refund terms, deposit treatment, tax status, insurance enrollment, and the user's individual circumstances.

contentImpacts.reason: Explain the current 10,000-yen fee, the 200,000-yen fee for covered applications from October 1, 2026, the application-date transition rule, payment timing, and applicable relief boundary.
Present current and future duration-based fees without collapsing counter, online, processing-charge, transition, or reduction distinctions.
Distinguish free special re-entry handling from paid ordinary single or multiple re-entry permits and identify channel differences.
Separate COE, consular visa, landing, and residence-procedure fee concepts and route readers to the applicable current schedule.
State that the COE application itself has no government fee while distinguishing school, agent, translation, delivery, and consular costs.
Audit remaining guidance for material official charges and useful current handoffs without manufacturing universal amounts for variable costs.

scopeBoundaries: Do not calculate an individual's taxes, insurance premiums, pension contributions, school budget, professional fees, or total relocation cost.
Do not copy volatile municipal or private prices merely to make an article appear complete; link to the responsible current schedule when a stable national amount does not exist.
Do not mix government charges, approved-agency handling fees, deposits, financial thresholds, and private prices in one unlabeled amount.
Do not show a future amount as already in force or hide the application-date transition rule.
Do not confer editorial-review status through this discovery or implementation pass.
unresolvedQuestions: Should effective-dated fees become a reusable typed content component in this pass, or remain carefully formatted article content until repeated use proves the schema necessary?
Which locally variable charges are important enough for pilot municipality supplements, and which should remain official-link handoffs?
Should source monitoring classify an amount or effective-date change as its own high-priority review reason before the broader critical-update workflow is used?

scopeApproval.note: The editor approved the official-fee and cost-disclosure workstream and a structured ChatGPT web research handoff pilot for independent comparison before implementation.
